# Paul Irving

## Overview

- **Age:** Ten years old, though looking younger  <sub>[v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c15 P11](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0011)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008)</sub>
- **Origin:** Boston, Massachusetts, United States  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c21 P83](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0083)</sub>
- **Role:** School pupil  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c7 P7](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0007)</sub>

## Appearance

Paul has a small build for his age with exquisite, delicate, and refined features. He is noted for his framed halo of naturally curly chestnut hair, delicious full lips, and big, expressive dark blue eyes. His countenance often carries a sober, grave, and meditative expression, which illuminates completely when he smiles.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c5 P21](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0021), [v2 c15 P11](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0011), [v2 c27 P7](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0007), [v2 c27 P29](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0029)_

## Personality

Paul is a deeply imaginative, rare, and sensitive boy described by those around him as a genius. He possesses flashes of uncanny insight and a grave, thoughtful spirit that makes him seem older than his years. He is polite, manly, cleanly, and fair-minded, yet holds a strong patriotic spirit and deep romantic sensibility.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c7 P7](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0007), [v2 c8 P32](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0032), [v2 c8 P52](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0052), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c23 P36](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0036), [v2 c27 P54](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0054)_

- Growing up to be as tall as his father  <sub>[v2 c27 P24](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0024)</sub>
- Eating all of his morning porridge to satisfy his grandmother  <sub>[v2 c15 P11](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0011)</sub>

## History

Paul Irving came from Boston to live with his grandmother on the shore road in Avonlea. On his first day attending Avonlea school, he quickly formed a deep bond of friendship and mutual understanding with his teacher, Anne Shirley. He established himself as an outstanding, popular pupil, even winning over local skeptics like Rachel Lynde despite his American background. Paul engaged in a drawn battle with fellow student St. Clair Donnell to defend the honor of the Stars and Stripes, leading to mutual respect between the two. He also developed a childhood crush on Gracie Andrews, once ducking his head into a spring to prove his hair was naturally curly when teased. When Anne resigned her teaching position to attend college, Paul was deeply heartbroken. Later, his father Stephen Irving arrived unexpectedly to visit, leading to a joyful reunion and Stephen's eventual reconciliation with Miss Lavendar Lewis.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c21 P83](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0083), [v2 c26 P34](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0034), [v2 c26 P35](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0035), [v2 c27 P7](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0007), [v2 c28 P21](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0021), [v2 c28 P26](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0026), [v2 c29 P1](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0001)_

## Background by volume

- Born in the United States to Stephen Irving  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c21 P83](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0083)</sub>
- Lost his mother three years prior to moving to Avonlea  <sub>[v2 c15 P4](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0004)</sub>
- Moved from Boston to Avonlea to live with his grandmother on the shore road  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c21 P83](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0083)</sub>

## Quotes

> Please, teacher, I found these in Mr. Wright’s field, and I came back to give them to you because I thought you were the kind of lady that would like them, and because . . . I like you, teacher.  <sub>[v2 c5 P21](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0021)</sub>

> You see, teacher, it’s just three years today since my little mother died. It’s such a long, long time but it hurts just as much as ever . . . and I miss her just as much as ever. Sometimes it seems to me that I just can’t bear it, it hurts so.  <sub>[v2 c15 P4](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0004)</sub>

> Grandma says father was brought up on porridge, and it certainly did work well in his case, for you ought to see the shoulders he has. But sometimes, I really think porridge will be the death of me.  <sub>[v2 c15 P11](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0011)</sub>

> That’s the beauty of dream-people . . . they stay any age you want them. You and my beautiful teacher and me myself are the only folks in the world that I know of that have dream-people. Isn’t it funny and nice we should all know each other?  <sub>[v2 c27 P62](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0062)</sub>

> Oh, Miss Shirley, you can’t think what has happened! Something so splendid. Father is here . . . just think of that! Father is here! Come right in. Father, this is my beautiful teacher. You know, father.  <sub>[v2 c28 P21](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0021)</sub>
